prompt:
Create ONE complete, polished front-cover image for a real British gardening paperback. Portrait aspect ratio 185:240 (37:48), flat front artwork viewed square on, filling the canvas, no mock-up, no spine, no perspective, no surrounding desk. Generate the photograph, composition and ALL finished lettering together as a single designed cover.

REFERENCE ROLES:
Image 1 is the user's actual photograph, the identity and content source. It shows author John Lennon facing the camera in his greenhouse, smiling gently and offering a metal colander full of ripe red tomatoes. Use THIS photograph and THIS person as the photographic centre of the cover. Preserve his recognisable facial features, age, thinning grey hair, short grey beard, expression, checked overshirt, olive T-shirt, natural hands, colander and tomatoes. Treat the person as an authentic photographic subject, not an illustrated or beautified replacement. Retain natural garden detail and strong ripe red fruit. Crop away irrelevant lower legs, pots and floor clutter. Reframe or extend garden/greenhouse background as necessary for the portrait cover and lettering, without inventing a different setting.
Image 2 is Anna Greenland's Grow Easy cover, supplied as a VISUAL DESIGN reference only. The user particularly admires its handsome warm yellow surround, big elegant lettering that overlaps the photographic field, readable hierarchy and inviting garden atmosphere. Draw on those design qualities to make an original cover for this user's book. Do not import its words, people, endorsements, logos or garden photo.

ART DIRECTION:
A sophisticated, warm, confidently designed UK gardening book that would look credible on a bookshop table. A rich golden-ochre / muted harvest-yellow surround, warm cream lettering, deep leafy greens and vivid natural red tomatoes. The book interior uses warm cream #fff8e9, forest green #064d32, rounded bold display headings and friendly humanist sans supporting type; let the cover belong to this colour world while having its own expressive editorial identity.
Compose a tall, generous photographic window with John and his abundant harvest substantial in the lower-middle of the cover. Integrate the large title into the upper photograph and coloured surround: elegant confident serif display lettering with organic softness and excellent spacing, striking but warm rather than formal. Let the title cross the photo boundary as a deliberate design move; avoid the previous generic layout of a separate heading panel stacked above an inset photograph. Use the reference's visual confidence and asymmetrical relationships without copying it literally.
Keep the face, both hands and the complete bowl easy to see. Plan calm leafy space behind the title; never write over John's eyes or mouth. Give the words their own clear hierarchy, with the title genuinely dominant and readable at small size. Balance the precise lettering against the rich living photograph. Use restrained, clean supporting type, comfortable margins and thoughtful negative space. No decorative vegetable cartoons, pictograms, stars, ribbons, reviews, badges, glossy effects, drop shadows or marketing slogans. Do not turn this into a YouTube thumbnail or an AI fantasy garden.

ONLY THESE EXACT WORDS ON THE COVER:
Title: The Vegetable Guru
Subtitle: Your at-a-glance growing companion
Author: John Lennon

Spell everything accurately. Integrate the subtitle legibly near the top and the author's name confidently towards the bottom, choosing the exact placements as part of the coherent composition. Preserve this title, subtitle and author; add no other text. Produce one finished front-cover concept, no comparison grid or alternatives. High-quality photographic detail and exceptionally well-rendered lettering.
originals: All prior covers, typography trials, photograph and interior proofs preserved.
